```{python}
# | echo: false

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Setup — one chart library (altair), one navy "consulting" theme, one palette,
# one table style. Tables are Quarto pipe tables so they inherit the deck's
# typography. Data pipeline reused from the (retired) dashboard.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import altair as alt

# --- consulting palette (matches the deck's navy look) ---------------------
FONT = "Helvetica Neue, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif"
NAVY, ACCENT, GREEN = "#1f3a5f", "#c4703a", "#4c8b6f"
INK, MUTED, GRID_C = "#1f2328", "#6b7280", "#e6e8eb"
RED = "#b0563b"
COHORT_RAMP = ["#a3c7e8", "#7aa9d0", "#4a86b8", "#2b5f8f", "#0d3b66"]
CHART_H = 280


@alt.theme.register("cba-deck", enable=True)
def _cba_deck() -> alt.theme.ThemeConfig:
    return {
        "config": {
            "background": "#ffffff",
            "font": FONT,
            "padding": {"left": 2, "top": 2, "right": 2, "bottom": 2},
            "view": {"stroke": None},
            "title": {
                "font": FONT, "fontSize": 13, "fontWeight": 700, "color": NAVY,
                "anchor": "start", "subtitleFont": FONT, "subtitleFontSize": 11,
                "subtitleColor": MUTED, "offset": 8,
            },
            "axis": {
                "labelFont": FONT, "titleFont": FONT, "labelFontSize": 11,
                "titleFontSize": 11, "titleFontWeight": 400, "labelColor": MUTED,
                "titleColor": MUTED, "domainColor": GRID_C, "tickColor": GRID_C,
                "grid": False,
            },
            "axisY": {"grid": True, "gridColor": GRID_C, "gridDash": [2, 2],
                      "domain": False, "ticks": False, "titlePadding": 6},
            "legend": {"labelFont": FONT, "titleFont": FONT, "labelFontSize": 11,
                       "titleFontSize": 11, "labelColor": MUTED, "titleColor": MUTED,
                       "symbolType": "square", "symbolSize": 90, "orient": "top",
                       "direction": "horizontal", "offset": 2},
            "header": {"labelFont": FONT, "labelFontSize": 11, "labelFontWeight": 700,
                       "labelColor": NAVY, "titleFont": FONT, "labelPadding": 2},
            "range": {"category": [NAVY, ACCENT, GREEN, "#8a6bb0", "#c9a227"],
                      "ordinal": COHORT_RAMP},
            "bar": {"color": NAVY},
            "line": {"color": NAVY, "strokeWidth": 2},
            "point": {"color": NAVY, "filled": True, "size": 30},
            "rule": {"color": MUTED},
            "text": {"font": FONT, "fontSize": 10, "fill": MUTED},
        }
    }


# --- Quarto pipe-table helper ---------------------------------------------
_FMT = {
    "money0": lambda v: f"${v:,.0f}", "money2": lambda v: f"${v:,.2f}",
    "num0": lambda v: f"{v:,.0f}", "num1": lambda v: f"{v:,.1f}",
    "num2": lambda v: f"{v:,.2f}", "pct0": lambda v: f"{v:.0%}",
    "pct1": lambda v: f"{v:.1%}",
    "signed_money0": lambda v: f"{'−' if v < 0 else ''}${abs(v):,.0f}",
}


def _cell(v, spec):
    if v is None or (isinstance(v, float) and np.isnan(v)):
        return ""
    if spec is None or isinstance(v, str):
        return str(v)
    return _FMT[spec](v)


def md_table(df, formats=None, left=(), bold_rows=()):
    formats = formats or {}
    cols = list(df.columns)
    head = "| " + " | ".join(str(c) for c in cols) + " |"
    rule = "| " + " | ".join(":--" if c in left else "--:" for c in cols) + " |"
    out = [head, rule]
    for i, (_, r) in enumerate(df.iterrows()):
        cells = [_cell(r[c], formats.get(c)) for c in cols]
        if i in bold_rows:
            cells = [f"**{c}**" if c else "" for c in cells]
        out.append("| " + " | ".join(cells) + " |")
    return "\n".join(out)


# --- data ------------------------------------------------------------------
cust_data = pd.read_csv("data/madrigal/cust_data_long.csv")
cust_data = (
    cust_data.assign(
        Spend=lambda x: (x["Spend"] * 100).round().astype("int64"),
        Profit=lambda x: (x["Profit"] * 100).round().astype("int64"),
    )
    .assign(
        **cust_data["YearQuarter"].str.extract(r"y(\d{4})_q(\d)")
        .rename(columns={0: "Year", 1: "Quarter"})
        .astype({"Year": "int32", "Quarter": "int8"})
    )
    .drop(columns="YearQuarter")
)

YEAR_PRIOR, YEAR_CURR = 2018, 2019
FOCUS_COHORT, FOCUS_COHORT_QTR = "y2016_q1", "Q1 2016"


def yearly_cust_data(df, year):
    return (
        df.query(f"Year == {year}").groupby("CustomerID", as_index=False)
        .agg(NumTrans=("NumTrans", "sum"), Spend=("Spend", "sum"),
             Profit=("Profit", "sum"))
        .assign(Spend=lambda x: (x["Spend"] / 100).astype("float32").round(2),
                Profit=lambda x: (x["Profit"] / 100).astype("float32").round(2))
    )


def customer_descriptives(df, metric):
    s = df[metric]
    mean = s.mean()
    return {"mean": mean, "median": s.median(), "min": s.min(), "max": s.max(),
            "pct_below_mean": (s < mean).mean(),
            "percentiles": s.quantile([i / 100 for i in range(5, 100, 5)])}


def create_bins_labels(bin_width, max_cutoff, min_cutoff=None):
    if min_cutoff is None:
        min_cutoff, lower_bins, lower_labels = 0, [], []
    else:
        lower_bins, lower_labels = [-np.inf], [f"<{min_cutoff}"]
    bins = lower_bins + list(range(min_cutoff, max_cutoff + bin_width, bin_width)) + [np.inf]
    labels = (lower_labels
              + [f"{i}-{i + bin_width}" for i in range(min_cutoff, max_cutoff, bin_width)]
              + [f"{max_cutoff}+"])
    return {"bins": bins, "labels": labels}


def create_distribution(df, column, bins, labels):
    d = (pd.cut(df[column], bins=bins, labels=labels, right=False)
         .value_counts().sort_index().reset_index()
         .rename(columns={"count": "Customers", column: "Range"}))
    d["Percent"] = d["Customers"] / d["Customers"].sum()
    return d.astype({"Range": str}).assign(Order=range(len(d)))


def decile_labels(df, value_col="Profit", n=10):
    d = df.sort_values(value_col, ascending=False, kind="stable").reset_index(drop=True)
    cents = np.round(d[value_col].to_numpy() * 100).astype(np.int64)
    cum = cents.cumsum()
    thresholds = np.arange(1, n) * cum[-1] / n
    boundaries = cents[np.searchsorted(cum, thresholds, side="right")]
    d["ProfitDecile"] = (n - np.searchsorted(boundaries[::-1], cents, side="left")).astype("int8")
    return d, thresholds / 100, boundaries / 100


DECILE_COLS = ["Decile", "% cust.", "% trans.", "% spend", "% profit",
               "Spend/cust.", "Profit/cust.", "AOF", "AOV", "Margin"]
DECILE_FMT = {"% cust.": "pct1", "% trans.": "pct1", "% spend": "pct1",
              "% profit": "pct1", "Spend/cust.": "money0", "Profit/cust.": "money0",
              "AOF": "num2", "AOV": "money0", "Margin": "pct1"}


def decile_report(df, decile_col):
    out = (df.groupby(decile_col, as_index=False)
           .agg(Customers=("CustomerID", "count"), Transactions=("NumTrans", "sum"),
                Spend=("Spend", "sum"), Profit=("Profit", "sum"))
           .assign(PctCust=lambda x: x["Customers"] / x["Customers"].sum(),
                   PctTrans=lambda x: x["Transactions"] / x["Transactions"].sum(),
                   PctSpend=lambda x: x["Spend"] / x["Spend"].sum(),
                   PctProfit=lambda x: x["Profit"] / x["Profit"].sum(),
                   AvgSpendCust=lambda x: x["Spend"] / x["Customers"],
                   AvgProfitCust=lambda x: x["Profit"] / x["Customers"],
                   AOF=lambda x: x["Transactions"] / x["Customers"],
                   AOV=lambda x: x["Spend"] / x["Transactions"],
                   AvgMargin=lambda x: x["Profit"] / x["Spend"])
           .drop(columns=["Customers", "Transactions", "Spend", "Profit"]))
    return out.rename(columns=dict(zip(out.columns, DECILE_COLS)))


# --- working datasets + headline numbers -----------------------------------
cust_data_2018 = yearly_cust_data(cust_data, YEAR_PRIOR)
cust_data_2019 = yearly_cust_data(cust_data, YEAR_CURR)
for _d in (cust_data_2018, cust_data_2019):
    _d["AvgSpendPerTrans"] = _d["Spend"] / _d["NumTrans"]
    _d["Margin"] = _d["Profit"] / _d["Spend"] * 100

cust_2018_2019 = (
    cust_data_2018.merge(cust_data_2019, on="CustomerID", how="outer",
                         suffixes=("_2018", "_2019"), indicator=True)
    .assign(Status=lambda df: df["_merge"].map(
        {"both": "Active both years", "left_only": "2018 only (lapsed)",
         "right_only": "2019 only (new/reactivated)"}))
    .drop(columns="_merge")
)

trans_bins = list(range(1, 11)) + [np.inf]
trans_labels = [str(i) for i in range(1, 10)] + ["10+"]

n_cust_2018, n_cust_2019 = len(cust_data_2018), len(cust_data_2019)
n_trans_2019 = int(cust_data_2019["NumTrans"].sum())
total_spend_2019 = cust_data_2019["Spend"].sum()
total_profit_2018 = cust_data_2018["Profit"].sum()
total_profit_2019 = cust_data_2019["Profit"].sum()
n_both = int((cust_2018_2019["Status"] == "Active both years").sum())
n_lapsed = int((cust_2018_2019["Status"] == "2018 only (lapsed)").sum())
n_new = int((cust_2018_2019["Status"] == "2019 only (new/reactivated)").sum())
one_and_done_pct = (cust_data_2019["NumTrans"] == 1).mean()
profit_yoy = (total_profit_2019 - total_profit_2018) / total_profit_2018
repeat_rate_2018 = n_both / n_cust_2018
aov_2019 = total_spend_2019 / n_trans_2019
mean_spend_2019 = cust_data_2019["Spend"].mean()
spend_stats = customer_descriptives(cust_data_2019, "Spend")
profit_stats = customer_descriptives(cust_data_2019, "Profit")
```

:::

## The average customer describes no one — value is concentrated, and its decay is driven by repeat buying

::: {.eyebrow}
Executive summary
:::

<ul class="points">
<li><b>Value is concentrated.</b> A small share of customers accounts for most transactions, spend, and profit — the base is not uniform.</li>
<li><b>The “average customer” describes no one.</b> Every behavioural measure is right-skewed, so the mean sits above the median and most customers fall below the mean.</li>
<li><b>Cohorts decay through fewer active buyers, not weaker spending.</b> Spend per active customer stays broadly flat; the base shrinks because fewer customers remain — so <b>repeat buying is the lever</b>.</li>
<li><b>Behaviour is stable and predictable</b> once heterogeneity is taken into account — the same patterns recur across periods and cohorts.</li>
</ul>

::: {.takeaway}
Manage the customer base as a portfolio: protect the high-value minority and lift repeat buying, rather than chase an “average” customer that does not exist.
:::

## One dataset, one profit identity — read every exhibit through its four factors

::: {.eyebrow}
Approach & data
:::

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**The data.** A 1% sample of **Madrigal**'s transaction records — 70,041 customers, aggregated to the quarter, for 16 quarters (Q1 2016 – Q4 2019). Each customer carries transactions, spend, profit, and an acquisition cohort.

The audit is **descriptive**: it summarises how customers behave; it does not forecast.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**One identity ties it together**

$$\text{Profit} = N_c \times \text{AOF} \times \text{AOV} \times \text{Margin}$$

(active customers × orders per customer × spend per order × margin)

Every result traces a change in profit to one of these factors — **fewer customers**, **less frequent orders**, **smaller orders**, or **thinner margins**.
:::
::::

# Lens 1 — How do customers differ from one another? {.divider background-color="#1f3a5f"}

## The average customer describes no one — every per-customer measure is right-skewed

::: {.eyebrow}
Lens 1 · Distributions · 2019
:::

```{python}
# | echo: false
cust_data_2019["TransBin"] = pd.cut(cust_data_2019["NumTrans"], bins=trans_bins,
                                    labels=trans_labels, right=False)
dist_defs = [
    ("Spend", "Spend", cust_data_2019, create_bins_labels(25, 1000)),
    ("Profit", "Profit", cust_data_2019, create_bins_labels(25, 500, min_cutoff=0)),
    ("Transactions", "NumTrans", cust_data_2019, {"bins": trans_bins, "labels": trans_labels}),
    ("Avg spend / txn", "AvgSpendPerTrans", cust_data_2019, create_bins_labels(25, 500)),
    ("Margin %", "Margin", cust_data_2019.query("Spend > 0"), create_bins_labels(5, 100, min_cutoff=0)),
]
_frames = [create_distribution(df, column=c, **b).assign(Metric=lbl)
           for lbl, c, df, b in dist_defs]
dist_long = pd.concat(_frames, ignore_index=True)
metric_order = [d[0] for d in dist_defs]

alt.Chart(dist_long).mark_bar().encode(
    x=alt.X("Range:N", sort=alt.EncodingSortField(field="Order"),
            axis=alt.Axis(labels=False, ticks=False, title=None)),
    y=alt.Y("Percent:Q", title="Customers", axis=alt.Axis(format="%")),
    tooltip=[alt.Tooltip("Metric:N"), alt.Tooltip("Range:N", title="Bin"),
             alt.Tooltip("Percent:Q", format=".1%")],
).properties(width=180, height=CHART_H).facet(
    facet=alt.Facet("Metric:N", title=None, sort=metric_order), columns=5
).resolve_scale(x="independent", y="independent")
```

::: {.takeaway}
About **`{python} f"{spend_stats['pct_below_mean']:.0%}"`** of customers spend below the mean and **`{python} f"{profit_stats['pct_below_mean']:.0%}"`** earn below the mean profit — a long right tail carries the base. **`{python} f"{one_and_done_pct:.0%}"`** bought exactly once.
:::

## The top deciles capture a disproportionate share of profit

::: {.eyebrow}
Lens 1 · Value concentration
:::

```{python}
# | echo: false
# | output: asis
_cust_profit = decile_labels(cust_data_2019, "Profit")[0]
print(md_table(decile_report(_cust_profit, "ProfitDecile"),
               formats=DECILE_FMT, left=["Decile"]))
```

::: {.takeaway}
Each decile is 10% of total profit — so decile 1 is a **handful** of customers and the bottom deciles are many customers contributing little or losing money.

## Spend, profit and the active count all grew — but beneath a large lapse-and-replace flow

```{python}

_order = ["Active both years", "2018 only (lapsed)", "2019 only (new/reactivated)"]
```

```{python}
# | echo: false
# | output: asis
_yoy = pd.DataFrame({
    "": ["Revenue", "Profit", "Active cust."],
    "2018": [f"${cust_data_2018['Spend'].sum():,.0f}", f"${total_profit_2018:,.0f}", f"{n_cust_2018:,}"],
    "2019": [f"${total_spend_2019:,.0f}", f"${total_profit_2019:,.0f}", f"{n_cust_2019:,}"],
    "Δ": [(total_spend_2019 - cust_data_2018['Spend'].sum()) / cust_data_2018['Spend'].sum(),

})
print(md_table(_yoy, formats={"Δ": "pct1"}, left=[""]))
```

Only **`{python} f"{repeat_rate_2018:.0%}"`** of 2018's buyers returned in 2019; the headline growth sits on top of heavy replacement.
:::
::::

::: {.takeaway}
The net change is small relative to the gross flows beneath it — sustaining profit depends on keeping **lapse** in check, not only on winning new customers.
:::

## How 2018 profit became 2019 profit — lapsed customers took out more than the surviving base lost

::: {.eyebrow}
Lens 2 · Profit bridge
:::

```{python}
# | echo: false
profit_by_group = cust_2018_2019.groupby("Status").agg(
    Y2018=("Profit_2018", lambda s: s.sum(min_count=1)),
    Y2019=("Profit_2019", lambda s: s.sum(min_count=1)))
both_18 = profit_by_group.loc["Active both years", "Y2018"]
both_19 = profit_by_group.loc["Active both years", "Y2019"]
only_18 = profit_by_group.loc["2018 only (lapsed)", "Y2018"]
only_19 = profit_by_group.loc["2019 only (new/reactivated)", "Y2019"]
tot_18, tot_19 = both_18 + only_18, both_19 + only_19

steps = pd.DataFrame([
    ("2018", 0.0, tot_18, "Total"),
    ("Lapsed", both_18, tot_18, "Decrease"),
    ("Both-years Δ", min(both_18, both_19), max(both_18, both_19),
     "Decrease" if both_19 < both_18 else "Increase"),
    ("New / react.", both_19, tot_19, "Increase"),
    ("2019", 0.0, tot_19, "Total"),
], columns=["Step", "Start", "End", "Kind"]).assign(
    Delta=lambda d: np.where(d["Kind"] == "Total", d["End"],
        np.where(d["Kind"] == "Decrease", -(d["End"] - d["Start"]), d["End"] - d["Start"])))
_ord = list(steps["Step"])
_bars = alt.Chart(steps).mark_bar(size=52).encode(
    x=alt.X("Step:N", sort=_ord, title=None, axis=alt.Axis(labelAngle=0)),
    y=alt.Y("Start:Q", title="Profit", axis=alt.Axis(format="$.2s")), y2="End:Q",
    color=alt.Color("Kind:N", scale=alt.Scale(
        domain=["Total", "Increase", "Decrease"], range=[MUTED, NAVY, RED]), legend=None),
    tooltip=[alt.Tooltip("Step:N"), alt.Tooltip("Delta:Q", format="$,.0f")])
_lab = alt.Chart(steps).mark_text(dy=-6, fontSize=11, color=INK).encode(
    x=alt.X("Step:N", sort=_ord), y="End:Q", text=alt.Text("Delta:Q", format="$,.3s"))
(_bars + _lab).properties(width="container", height=CHART_H)
```

::: {.takeaway}
The both-years group shrank; new customers more than covered it. **Replacement, not the surviving base, drives the year-on-year line.**
:::

# Lens 3 — How does a single cohort evolve? {.divider background-color="#1f3a5f"}

## Cohort revenue decays through fewer active buyers — not weaker spending

::: {.eyebrow}
Lens 3 · Revenue decomposition · Q1 2016 cohort
:::

```{python}
# | echo: false
cohort_q = (cust_data.query("Cohort == 'y2016_q1'").groupby(["Year", "Quarter"])
            .agg(ActiveCust=("CustomerID", "count"), TotalTrans=("NumTrans", "sum"),
                 TotalSpend=("Spend", "sum"), TotalProfit=("Profit", "sum")))
cohort_size = cohort_q.xs((2016, 1))["ActiveCust"]
cohort_q = cohort_q.assign(
    Pct_Active=cohort_q["ActiveCust"] / cohort_size,
    ASPAC=cohort_q["TotalSpend"] / cohort_q["ActiveCust"] / 100,
    AOF=cohort_q["TotalTrans"] / cohort_q["ActiveCust"],
    AOV=cohort_q["TotalSpend"] / cohort_q["TotalTrans"] / 100)
_labels = {"Pct_Active": "% active", "ASPAC": "Spend per active", "AOF": "AOF", "AOV": "AOV"}
comp_long = (cohort_q.reset_index()
    .assign(Period=lambda d: (d["Year"] - 2016) * 4 + (d["Quarter"] - 1))
    .melt(id_vars="Period", value_vars=list(_labels), var_name="Component", value_name="Value")
    .assign(Component=lambda d: d["Component"].map(_labels)))

alt.Chart(comp_long).mark_line(point=alt.OverlayMarkDef(size=25, filled=True)).encode(
    x=alt.X("Period:Q", title="Quarters since acquisition", axis=alt.Axis(tickMinStep=4)),
    y=alt.Y("Value:Q", title=None),
    tooltip=[alt.Tooltip("Component:N"), alt.Tooltip("Period:Q", title="Quarter"),
             alt.Tooltip("Value:Q", format=",.2f")],
).properties(width=200, height=CHART_H).facet(
    facet=alt.Facet("Component:N", title=None, sort=list(_labels.values())), columns=4
).resolve_scale(y="independent")
```

::: {.takeaway}
The customers who remain keep behaving normally; the base shrinks because **fewer of them remain** — the lever is repeat buying, not spend stimulation.
:::

## Most repeat buying is decided early — the second-purchase curve flattens within a year

::: {.eyebrow}
Lens 3 · Time to second purchase · Q1 2016 cohort
:::

```{python}
# | echo: false
q_matrix = (cust_data.query("Cohort == 'y2016_q1'").sort_values(["Year", "Quarter"])
    .pivot_table(index="CustomerID", columns=["Year", "Quarter"], values="NumTrans",
                 aggfunc="sum", fill_value=0))
q_periods = [f"Y{y} Q{q}" for y, q in q_matrix.columns]
_first = q_matrix.columns.min()
_thr = pd.Series(1, index=q_matrix.columns).mask(q_matrix.columns != _first, 0)
_second = q_matrix.gt(_thr).cummax(axis=1)
cum_pct = _second.mean()
never_second = 1 - cum_pct.iloc[-1]
second_df = pd.DataFrame({"Period": q_periods, "Cumulative": cum_pct.to_numpy()})

alt.Chart(second_df).mark_area(line={"color": NAVY, "strokeWidth": 2}, opacity=0.15, color=NAVY).encode(
    x=alt.X("Period:N", sort=q_periods, title=None, axis=alt.Axis(labelAngle=-45)),
    y=alt.Y("Cumulative:Q", title="Share of cohort", axis=alt.Axis(format=".0%"),
            scale=alt.Scale(domain=[0, 1])),
    tooltip=[alt.Tooltip("Period:N"), alt.Tooltip("Cumulative:Q", format=".1%")],
).properties(width="container", height=CHART_H,
    title=alt.TitleParams(f"{1 - never_second:.0%} of the cohort ever came back — most within a year",
        subtitle="The curve flattens hard after the first year: a second purchase happens early or not at all", anchor="start"))
```

::: {.takeaway}
Early experience is decisive — invest in the **first few quarters** of a customer's life, where the repeat decision is actually made.
:::

# Lens 4 — How does the base grow and stay healthy? {.divider background-color="#1f3a5f"}

## Growth is bought with acquisition — every cohort's contribution decays a year later

::: {.eyebrow}
Lens 4 · Annual profit by acquisition cohort
:::

```{python}
# | echo: false
cohort_year = (cust_data.assign(
        CohortYear=lambda d: np.where(d["Cohort"] == "pre_y2016", "pre-2016", d["Cohort"].str[1:5]))
    .groupby(["Year", "CohortYear"], as_index=False).agg(Profit=("Profit", "sum"))
    .assign(Profit=lambda d: d["Profit"] / 100))
cohort_order = ["pre-2016", "2016", "2017", "2018", "2019"]
alt.Chart(cohort_year).mark_bar().encode(
    x=alt.X("Year:O", title=None, axis=alt.Axis(labelAngle=0)),
    y=alt.Y("Profit:Q", title="Profit", axis=alt.Axis(format="$.2s")),
    color=alt.Color("CohortYear:N", sort=cohort_order,
        scale=alt.Scale(domain=cohort_order, range=COHORT_RAMP),
        legend=alt.Legend(title="Acquired")),
    order=alt.Order("CohortYear:N", sort="descending"),
    tooltip=[alt.Tooltip("Year:O"), alt.Tooltip("CohortYear:N", title="Cohort"),
             alt.Tooltip("Profit:Q", format="$,.0f")],
).properties(width="container", height=CHART_H + 20)
```

::: {.takeaway}
Each year's profit rests on a **stack of older cohorts** whose contribution roughly halves a year on; new acquisition tops it up. A healthy base carries a thick still-active tail — repeat buying compounds.
:::

## Four moves follow directly from the audit {background-color="#ffffff"}

::: {.eyebrow}
Implications
:::

<ul class="points">
<li><b>Treat the base as a portfolio.</b> Segment by value and manage the high-value minority explicitly — the average hides them.</li>
<li><b>Make repeat buying the first lever.</b> Cohort decay is driven by fewer active customers, so small repeat-buying gains compound across every cohort.</li>
<li><b>Win the second purchase early.</b> Repeat behaviour is largely set in the first few quarters — invest in early-life experience.</li>
<li><b>Acquire more of the right customers.</b> Per-customer behaviour is stable, so growth comes mainly from adding customers like the ones you keep.</li>
</ul>

::: {.takeaway}
None of these require an “average customer.” They require managing a heterogeneous base **by value and by age**.
:::

# Appendix {.divider background-color="#1f3a5f"}

## A definitions note — keep the two “average transaction” numbers apart

::: {.eyebrow}
Appendix · Method
:::

<ul class="points">
<li><b>AOV — ratio of totals.</b> Total spend ÷ total transactions (≈ $`{python} f"{aov_2019:,.0f}"`). A <b>transaction-weighted</b> average, so frequent buyers dominate it.</li>
<li><b>Mean of per-customer averages.</b> Average each customer's own spend-per-transaction, then average across customers (≈ $`{python} f"{cust_data_2019['AvgSpendPerTrans'].mean():,.0f}"`). Every customer counts equally, so one-and-done buyers pull it up.</li>
</ul>

The two are equal only if every customer transacts the same number of times, which never happens. Here the weighted figure sits **below** the unweighted one, so heavier buyers have smaller baskets than light buyers.

::: {.source}
Convention used throughout: “AOV” always means the transaction-weighted ratio of totals · Source: Madrigal transaction sample, 2016–2019
:::

## A wording note — “retention” vs “repeat-buying rate” vs “% cohort active”

::: {.eyebrow}
Appendix · Method
:::

<ul class="points">
<li><b>Why not “retention” here.</b> Madrigal is <b>noncontractual</b> — a customer who skips a period has not necessarily left. “Retention” properly describes contractual renewal / survival, where a cancellation is actually observed; using it here invites false “we lost them” conclusions.</li>
<li><b>% of cohort active.</b> The share of a cohort that buys in a period — <b>unconditional</b>, and it includes one-time buyers (the diagonal of the cohort chart).</li>
<li><b>Repeat-buying rate.</b> The <b>conditional</b> quantity — the share of customers active in one period who buy again the next.</li>
<li><b>Carryover.</b> For value, a cohort's profit in one year relative to the year before (what the profit-flow chart annotates).</li>
</ul>

The three are not interchangeable; only in a contractual setting does “retention rate” have a single, well-defined meaning.

::: {.source}
After Fader, Hardie & Ross, *The Customer-Base Audit* (2022), Ch. 9 — “Be Wary of the ‘R’ Word”
:::
